chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a group of the Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and asked him to appoint them over the charities of the livestock, saying, 'Let this portion which Allah has made for the workers upon it be for us, for we are more deserving of it.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'O sons of Abdul Muttalib! Indeed, charity is not permissible for me nor for you, but I have been promised intercession.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, he (peace be upon him and his family) has indeed been promised it. So what is your opinion, O sons of Abdul Muttalib, when I take hold of the ring of the door of Paradise? Do you see me giving preference to others over you?'

key_terms.السَّهْمُ: The portion (specifically the share of the collector)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Banu Hashim ask to collect charity and what was the Prophet's response regarding their eligibility?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between the general prohibition of sadaqah for the Prophet and his family (Banu Hashim) and the specific exception of the 'portion of the collector' (al-sahm al-amil), which they could claim as workers. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links this material privilege to the spiritual promise of intercession (shafa'ah), emphasizing that the Prophet’s priority for his family in Paradise is a certainty derived from divine promise. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Ahl al-Bayt’s exclusion from general charity does not diminish their unique status or their right to specific allocations.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, and Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ays Bin Al Qasim,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘A group of people from the Clan of Hashim came over to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. So they asked him<sup>saww</sup> that he<sup>saww</sup> should utilise them upon the (collection of the) charities of the livestock, and they said, ‘Can there happen to be for us this portion which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made it to be for the workers over it, so we are the closes with it’. So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O sons of Abdul Muttalib<sup>as</sup>! The charity is neither Permissible for me, nor for you all, but I<sup>saww</sup> have been Promised the intercession’.

Then Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has been Promised it. So what is your thinking, O sons of Abdul Muttalib<sup>asws</sup>! When I<sup>asws</sup> grab the ring of the door of the Paradise, do you see me<sup>asws</sup> giving preference to others over you all?’
en.sarwar: 1. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Iys ibn al-Qasim who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once certain people of Banu Hashim came to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and asked him to appoint them for collecting zakat on cattle. Therefore, the share of zakat collectors should be given to them. The Messenger of Allah said, ‘O children of ‘Abd al-Muttalib, receiving zakat is not lawful for me or for you. However, it is promised that I will have the privilege to intercede before the Lord to save from the fire whomever I will choose.’

-Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said that ‘by Allah, He (Allah) has promised His Messenger to have such a privilege,’- ‘What do you then think, children of ‘Abd al-Muttalib, when I have my hands on the doorknob of Paradise, will I give preference to others beside you?’ he (the Messenger of Allah) explained.”
